habitat: Highly gregarious in dry grassland or open bushveld, often with cattle. Flocks feed on the ground. Breeding colonies build hundreds of nests in thorn bushes. Nomadic when not breeding.
summary: A common resident. A pale starling. Non-breeding males and females are whitish, and the white rump shows in flight. The breeding male's head may have yellow-and-black skin and wattles, and the tail is black. The call is a rasping squeak. The Kemp name Wattled Starling and the code VB were left unchanged.

head.pattern: Male and female are whitish when not breeding.

upperparts.pattern: Whitish. The white rump shows in flight.

head.pattern: Breeding male head ornamented with black and yellow skin, plus wattles, or with only the wattles.

viewNotes.note: Whitish, and drab compared with the breeding male.
Head ornamented with black and yellow skin and wattles.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A rasping, squeaky sound. The grade A call is from Kruger. The filename is XC489190-Wattled Starlings KNP 190415-075512.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Whitish is not stored as a vocabulary colour. The grade A call is from Kruger. The Kemp code VB was left unchanged.
